title: Isaiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Isaiah 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Lord sitting upon a throne
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord sitting upon a throne
questions.explanation: This event appears first in the chapter, as stated in Isaiah 6:1.

questions.question: What did the seraphims use to cover their faces?
questions.explanation: The seraphims covered their faces with twain (two) of their six wings, as stated in Isaiah 6:2.

questions.question: What did one seraphim cry to another?
options: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts
The whole earth is full of his glory
Mine eyes have seen the King
questions.correctAnswer: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: This phrase is what one seraphim cried to another, as stated in Isaiah 6:3.

questions.question: What happened to the posts of the door at the voice of him that cried?
questions.explanation: The posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, as stated in Isaiah 6:4.

questions.question: What filled the house after the voice cried?
questions.explanation: The house was filled with smoke, as stated in Isaiah 6:4.

questions.question: What did Isaiah declare about himself?
options: I am a man of clean lips
Woe is me! for I am undone
questions.correctAnswer: Woe is me! for I am undone
questions.explanation: Isaiah said, 'Woe is me! for I am undone,' as stated in Isaiah 6:5.

questions.question: Why did Isaiah feel undone?
options: Because he was a man of unclean lips
Because he was in a holy place
Because he had seen the King
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was a man of unclean lips
questions.explanation: Isaiah felt undone because he was a man of unclean lips, as stated in Isaiah 6:5.

questions.question: In the vision, who is sitting upon the throne?
questions.explanation: The Lord is described as sitting upon a throne in Isaiah 6:1.

questions.question: What did Isaiah see in the year that King Uzziah died?
questions.explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne in the year that King Uzziah died, as stated in Isaiah 6:1.

questions.question: How many wings did each seraphim have?
questions.explanation: Each seraphim had six wings, as stated in Isaiah 6:2.

questions.question: What is filled with the glory of the Lord?
questions.explanation: The whole earth is full of His glory, as stated in Isaiah 6:3.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah felt he was among a people of unclean lips.
questions.explanation: Isaiah stated that he dwells in the midst of a people of unclean lips in Isaiah 6:5.

questions.question: True or False: The seraphims are described as having eight wings.
questions.explanation: The seraphims are described as having six wings, not eight, as stated in Isaiah 6:2.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah saw the Lord after the death of King Uzziah.
questions.explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord in the year that King Uzziah died, not after his death, as stated in Isaiah 6:1.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that the Lord was angry with Isaiah.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention that the Lord was angry with Isaiah; it focuses on Isaiah's feelings of being undone, as stated in Isaiah 6:5.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did one of the seraphims bring to Isaiah?
questions.explanation: The seraphim flew to Isaiah with a live coal in his hand, taken from the altar (Isaiah 6:6).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 6:7 promise will happen if someone has their iniquity taken away?
options: They will be filled with joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:7 states that having iniquity taken away results in sin being purged, which means forgiveness.

questions.question: What was Isaiah's response when he heard the Lord say, 'Whom shall I send?'
questions.explanation: Isaiah responded to the Lord's call with a willingness to be sent (Isaiah 6:8).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 6:9, what message was Isaiah commanded to deliver to the people?
options: Hear ye indeed, but understand not
Prepare for the coming of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Hear ye indeed, but understand not
questions.explanation: The Lord instructed Isaiah to tell the people that they would hear but not understand (Isaiah 6:9).

questions.question: What effect does Isaiah 6:10 say the message will have on the people's hearts?
options: Their hearts will be made soft
Their hearts will be made fat
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts will be made fat
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:10 indicates that the message will harden the hearts of the people, making them unresponsive.

questions.question: What does Isaiah acknowledge about himself in Isaiah 6:5?
options: He is a man of clean lips
He is a man of unclean lips
He is a prophet of God
questions.correctAnswer: He is a man of unclean lips
questions.explanation: Isaiah expresses his unworthiness by declaring he is a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5).

questions.question: Why does Isaiah consider himself 'undone'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah feels undone because he has seen the King, the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 6:5).

questions.question: What did the seraphim use to touch Isaiah's lips?
questions.explanation: The seraphim laid a live coal upon Isaiah's mouth to signify the purging of his sin (Isaiah 6:7).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'shut their eyes' in Isaiah 6:10 imply about the people's spiritual condition?
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the people are spiritually blind and unable to perceive the truth (Isaiah 6:10).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 6:3 highlight about the nature of God?
questions.explanation: The seraphim proclaim the holiness of God, emphasizing His pure and exalted nature (Isaiah 6:3).

questions.question: What is the significance of the altar from which the seraphim took the coal?
options: It is a place of prayer
It is a place of worship
questions.explanation: The altar symbolizes the place of sacrifice, where atonement is made, which is significant in Isaiah's cleansing (Isaiah 6:6).

questions.question: What can we learn from Isaiah's willingness to respond to God's call?
questions.explanation: Isaiah's response teaches us the importance of being open and available to God's call (Isaiah 6:8).

questions.question: Is it necessary to understand everything before responding to God's call?
questions.explanation: Isaiah responded to God's call despite not fully understanding the outcome, showing that understanding is not always necessary.

questions.question: Can sin be purged without a response to God's cleansing?
questions.explanation: Isaiah had to receive the cleansing for his sin to be purged, indicating the necessity of response (Isaiah 6:7).

questions.question: Does the message to the people guarantee they will understand it?
questions.explanation: The message delivered by Isaiah is specifically stated to be heard but not understood (Isaiah 6:9).

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: What does the Lord say will happen until the cities are wasted without inhabitant?
options: The land will be utterly desolate
questions.correctAnswer: The land will be utterly desolate
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:11 states that the Lord answered, 'Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,' indicating that desolation is the consequence until the cities are destroyed.

questions.question: What does the LORD do according to Isaiah 6:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:12 explains that 'the LORD have removed men far away,' indicating a separation of people from their homeland.

questions.question: What will happen to the holy seed according to Isaiah 6:13?
options: It shall be the substance thereof
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be the substance thereof
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:13 states, 'so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof,' indicating the enduring nature of the holy seed despite the destruction.

questions.question: What is one consequence mentioned in Isaiah 6:11?
options: The houses will be without man
questions.correctAnswer: The houses will be without man
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:11 includes the phrase 'and the houses without man,' signifying the extent of desolation that will occur.

questions.question: What does the term 'great forsaking' refer to in Isaiah 6:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:12 mentions 'a great forsaking in the midst of the land,' which indicates a divine judgment leading to abandonment.

questions.question: In Isaiah 6:13, what analogy is used for the holy seed?
options: A teil tree and an oak
questions.correctAnswer: A teil tree and an oak
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:13 compares the holy seed to 'a teil tree, and as an oak,' illustrating its strength and resilience.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'kodesh' in Isaiah 6:13 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Kodesh' in Hebrew refers to holiness, aligning with the theme of the holy seed mentioned in Isaiah 6:13.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Isaiah 6:3 with the phrase 'Holy, holy, holy'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Holy, holy, holy' in Isaiah 6:3 is an example of repetition, emphasizing the holiness of the Lord.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of desolation seen in Isaiah 6:11?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 25:11 speaks of desolation and destruction, echoing the theme found in Isaiah 6:11 regarding the cities being wasted.

questions.question: Which other passage in the New Testament connects to the idea of spiritual blindness in Isaiah 6:10?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:14 references spiritual blindness, similar to the condition described in Isaiah 6:10, indicating a lack of understanding.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Isaiah 6:11?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:10, which precedes verse 11, contains the Lord's command to Isaiah, followed by Isaiah's question in verse 11, showing his awareness of the dire situation.

questions.question: What is the primary theme of Isaiah 6:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:12 indicates a 'great forsaking,' which reflects the theme of judgment upon the people of Israel.

questions.question: In Isaiah 6:13, what does the mention of trees symbolize?
questions.explanation: The reference to 'a teil tree, and as an oak' in Isaiah 6:13 symbolizes life and endurance, representing the sustenance that the holy seed will provide.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah hears the voice of the Lord asking, 'Whom shall I send?'
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:8 states that Isaiah heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send?' confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord's response to Isaiah's question is that He will save all the people.
questions.explanation: The Lord's response indicates desolation and forsaking rather than salvation, as seen in Isaiah 6:11-12.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 6:5 teach about human sin?
options: Human sin causes a sense of unworthiness before God
Human sin is insignificant compared to divine holiness
Human sin can be overcome by human effort alone
Human sin is only external and does not affect the heart
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin causes a sense of unworthiness before God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:5 shows the prophet's reaction to seeing the Lord's holiness, causing him to recognize his own uncleanness and sinfulness, thus teaching the doctrine that human sin results in a deep sense of unworthiness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 6:7 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation involves the cleansing and purging of sin by divine intervention
Salvation is a gradual human process without divine involvement
Salvation is only a future hope with no present application
Salvation requires ritual sacrifices performed by humans
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves the cleansing and purging of sin by divine intervention
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:7 describes a seraph laying a live coal on Isaiah's lips, symbolizing that his iniquity is taken away and sin purged, indicating that salvation includes divine cleansing of sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 6:9 teach about human response to God's word?
options: God’s judgment includes judicial hardening of those who reject His message
God’s word is always immediately understood and accepted
Humans can choose to perfectly understand God without divine help
God’s message is only for the holy and excludes sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment includes judicial hardening of those who reject His message
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:9 commands to tell the people that they will hear but not understand, see but not perceive, which teaches the doctrine of judicial hardening in response to persistent rejection.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Isaiah 6:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:3 repeats 'Holy, holy, holy' to emphasize the absolute holiness of the LORD of hosts, demonstrating His divine attribute of holiness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 6:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:8 shows the Lord’s sovereign authority in calling and sending servants, demonstrating His divine sovereignty over the mission of His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 6 connect to the theme of prophetic commissioning found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the calling of prophets who act as mediators of divine holiness
It rejects the role of prophecy in Israel's history
It shows that prophets only speak private messages with no public relevance
It emphasizes that prophets are self-appointed without divine call
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the calling of prophets who act as mediators of divine holiness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:8 depicts the prophet’s commissioning after cleansing, which parallels other biblical prophetic call narratives where God calls prophets to mediate His holiness and message.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is evident between Isaiah 6:13 and the concept of remnant theology?
options: It teaches that a holy remnant will survive judgment to continue God’s purposes
It rejects the idea of any surviving faithful remnant
It teaches that all Israel will be saved unconditionally
It focuses only on individual salvation without corporate significance
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that a holy remnant will survive judgment to continue God’s purposes
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:13 speaks of a tenth remaining as a holy seed, which aligns with the biblical doctrine of a remnant preserved by God to fulfill His covenantal promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Isaiah 6:5 and Isaiah 6:7 teach about sanctification?
options: Recognition of sin leads to divine cleansing and sanctification
Sanctification is purely a human ethical achievement
Sin is not relevant to the process of sanctification
Sanctification happens before the recognition of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Recognition of sin leads to divine cleansing and sanctification
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:5 reveals the prophet’s awareness of sin, and 6:7 describes divine cleansing by a live coal, together teaching that sanctification begins with recognition of sin followed by divine purging.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 6:9 and Isaiah 6:10 teach about human spiritual blindness?
options: God judicially hardens the hearts of those who reject His message
Spiritual blindness is accidental and not related to God’s will
All people can see and understand God’s word without exception
God’s message always results in immediate repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God judicially hardens the hearts of those who reject His message
questions.explanation: Verses 6:9–10 describe God instructing Isaiah to make the people’s hearts fat and eyes shut, teaching the doctrine of judicial hardening in response to persistent rejection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 6:11 and Isaiah 6:12 teach about divine judgment?
options: Judgment results in desolation and exile as a consequence of sin
Judgment is symbolic and does not affect physical realities
Judgment is temporary and without lasting effect
Judgment spares the unrepentant and only punishes foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment results in desolation and exile as a consequence of sin
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:11–12 depict cities wasted, houses empty, and great forsaking in the land, teaching that divine judgment entails desolation and exile.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Isaiah 6:9–10 teaches God punishes people arbitrarily by hardening their hearts. What does Isaiah 6:9–10 actually teach?
options: God judicially hardens those who persistently reject His message after repeated warnings
God punishes without cause or prior warning
God’s hardening is random and unrelated to human response
God’s message is universally accepted with no rejection
questions.correctAnswer: God judicially hardens those who persistently reject His message after repeated warnings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:9–10 shows that God’s hardening is a judicial response to persistent rejection, not arbitrary punishment without cause.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 6:2 teach about the nature of heavenly beings and worship?
options: Heavenly beings express reverence and cover their faces and feet in God's presence
Heavenly beings appear as human-like and unhidden
Worship in heaven is silent and without expression
Seraphim have only two wings and do not fly
questions.correctAnswer: Heavenly beings express reverence and cover their faces and feet in God's presence
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:2 describes seraphim with six wings, covering their faces and feet, indicating reverence and awe in worship before God’s holiness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 6:4 specifically demonstrate in relation to God’s presence?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:4 describes the doorposts shaking and the temple filling with smoke at the voice of the one crying holy, illustrating God’s majestic presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 6:1 and Isaiah 6:13 teach about God's kingship and covenant faithfulness?
options: God remains sovereign and preserves a faithful remnant despite judgment
God's kingship is temporary and dependent on Israel's obedience
God abandons His covenant people after judgment
God's presence is absent from the temple during judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God remains sovereign and preserves a faithful remnant despite judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:1 presents the LORD enthroned in majesty, and 6:13 speaks of a holy seed remaining, showing God's sovereign kingship and covenant faithfulness in preserving a remnant.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 6:6–7 contribute to the doctrine of sanctification through divine means rather than human effort?
options: It shows that sanctification is initiated by God cleansing the sinner’s lips
It implies sanctification is achieved by human ritual alone
It suggests sanctification is unnecessary for the prophet
It teaches sanctification is only future and not present
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that sanctification is initiated by God cleansing the sinner’s lips
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:6–7 describes a seraph touching Isaiah’s lips with a live coal from the altar, symbolizing that sanctification is an act of divine cleansing, not human merit.
